name: Lloyd Roberts
role: Pioneer cattleman and cattle buyer, Sloping Bottom ranch
bio: The Cow Boy introduced Lloyd Roberts in February 1884 as a pioneer cattleman who had driven the first herd into Bismarck, Standing Rock and the Bad Lands, and friends gave a dance in his honor at the Hotel de Mores. His ranch lay twelve miles up the river, later called the Sloping Bottom ranch. Each year he went east, usually to St. Cloud, Minn., with Daniel Friedman and others, to buy cattle for delivery to local ranchers and to buyers at Glendive; in June 1884 he and Howard Eaton brought in a thousand head for the Badger cattle company. In late August 1884 he and two others killed three buffalo from a herd south of town, and in October 1885 he finished grading for the new stock yards and took purchased buffalo to Rapid City. In 1886 he delivered a herd for Aleck Connell's Cave Hills ranch and spent the fall buying stock in St. Cloud and Cheyenne.
